text: Jerubbaal—that is, Gideon—rose early, and all the people with him, and they camped beside the spring of Harod. The camp of Midian lay to the north of them, by the hill of Moreh in the valley.
The LORD said to Gideon, "You have too many people with you for me to give Midian into their hands. Israel might boast against me and say, 'My own hand saved me.'
Now then, announce to the people: 'Whoever is afraid and trembling may turn back and leave Mount Gilead.'" Twenty-two thousand of the people turned back, and ten thousand remained.

Then the LORD said to Gideon, "There are still too many. Take them down to the water, and I will sift them for you there. The one I tell you shall go with you, he shall go; and anyone I tell you shall not go with you, he shall not go."

So he took the people down to the water, and the LORD said to Gideon, "Everyone who laps up the water with his tongue as a dog laps, set him apart on one side; and everyone who kneels down to drink, set him on the other."

versions.text: So he took the people down to the water, and the LORD said to Gideon, "Set apart by himself everyone who laps up the water with his tongue as a dog laps, and likewise everyone who kneels down to drink."
versions.explanation: The word "likewise" wrongly implies the kneelers are grouped with the lappers, whereas the point of the Hebrew (elliptical clause) is that the two groups are separated from each other. The following verses show the lappers alone were chosen.

text: The number of those who lapped, hand to mouth, was three hundred men. All the rest of the people knelt down to drink the water.
The LORD said to Gideon, "With the three hundred men who lapped I will save you and give Midian into your hand. Let all the others go, each to his own place."

So the three hundred took the people's provisions and their trumpets, and Gideon sent all the other Israelites home to their tents, keeping only the three hundred men. Now the camp of Midian lay below him in the valley.
That same night the LORD said to him, "Get up, go down against the camp, for I have given it into your hand.
But if you are afraid to go down, take your servant Purah with you to the camp,

and listen to what they are saying. Afterward your hands will be strengthened, and you will go down against the camp." So he went down with his servant Purah to the outposts of the armed men in the camp.

versions.text: and listen to what they are saying. Afterward your hands will be strengthened to go down against the camp." So he went down with his servant Purah to the outposts of the armed men in the camp.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has two coordinated statements—hands strengthened, then the descent—rather than making the descent the purpose of the strengthening.

text: The Midianites, the Amalekites, and all the people of the east lay sprawled across the valley, as thick as locusts, and their camels were beyond counting, like the sand on the seashore.

When Gideon arrived, a man was telling his comrade a dream. "Listen," he said, "I had a dream: a round loaf of barley bread came tumbling into the camp of Midian. It struck a tent, and the tent turned over and collapsed."
His comrade answered, "That can be nothing but the sword of Gideon son of Joash, the Israelite. God has given Midian and the whole camp into his hand."
When Gideon heard the dream and its interpretation, he bowed down in worship. He returned to the camp of Israel and said, "Get up! The LORD has given the camp of Midian into your hands."
He divided the three hundred men into three companies and put a trumpet in every man's hand, along with an empty jar and a torch inside the jar.
He told them, "Watch me and do the same. When I reach the edge of the camp, do exactly as I do.
When I and all who are with me blow our trumpets, then you blow yours all around the camp and shout, 'For the LORD and for Gideon!'"

Gideon and the hundred men with him came to the edge of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch, just after the guard had been changed. They blew their trumpets and smashed the jars in their hands.

The three companies blew their trumpets and shattered their jars. Holding the torches in their left hands and the trumpets in their right hands to blow, they shouted, "A sword for the LORD and for Gideon!"
Each man held his position around the camp, while the whole camp ran, crying out and fleeing.

versions.text: Each man held his position around the camp, while the whole camp broke into panic, running and fleeing.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has three verbs: they ran, they cried out (וַיָּרִיעוּ), and they fled. The rendering "broke into panic" replaces the shouting with an interpretive paraphrase and drops the element of outcry.

text: As the three hundred trumpets sounded, the LORD set every man's sword against his comrade throughout the camp, and the army fled as far as Beth Shittah toward Zererah, to the edge of Abel Meholah near Tabbath.
The Israelites were called out from Naphtali, Asher, and all Manasseh, and they pursued the Midianites.

Gideon also sent messengers throughout the hill country of Ephraim, saying, "Come down against Midian and seize the waters ahead of them as far as Beth Barah, and the Jordan as well." So all the men of Ephraim were called out, and they seized the waters as far as Beth Barah, and the Jordan.

They captured the two Midianite commanders, Oreb and Zeeb. They killed Oreb at the rock of Oreb and Zeeb at the winepress of Zeeb, and they pursued the Midianites. Then they brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon on the other side of the Jordan.
